simple.meaning: כֶּלֶא (keleʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a prison.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 22:27. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כֶּלֶא (H3608) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: כֶּלֶא (keleʼ) / H3608 is traced through 1 Kings 22:27, 2 Kings 17:4, 2 Kings 25:27, 2 Kings 25:29 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H3608. kele כֶּ֫לֶא noun [masculine] confinement, restraint, imprisonment ; — absolute ׳כ 1Kin 22:27 6 t.; suffix כִּלְאוֺ 2Kin 25:29 ; Jer 52:33 ; plural כְּלָאִים Isa 42:22 ; — confinement , in combination (ה)כ ׳בֵּית (compare Assyrian bit kili , prison , Dl HWB 328 ) 1Kin 22:27 2Chr 18:26 ; 2Kin 17:4 ; Jer 37:15 , 18 ; Isa 42:7 ; כְלָאִים בָּֽתֵּי 42:22 (compare בַּיִת 1 ( ε ) (2) p. 109 above; see also כלוא below); כִלְאוֺ בִּנְדֵי 2Kin 25:29 = Jer 52:33 garments of imprisonment = prison-garb.

occurrences.englishText: Say, ‘The king says, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.” ’ ”

The king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea; for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and offered no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year. Therefore the king of Assyria seized him, and bound him in prison.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
and changed his prison garments. Jehoiachin ate bread before him continually all the days of his life;
and say, ‘The king says, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.” ’ ”
But this is a robbed and plundered people.
The princes were angry with Jeremiah, and struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe; for they had made that the prison.
Moreover Jeremiah said to king Zedekiah, “How have I sinned against you, against your servants, or against this people, that you have put me in prison?
and changed his prison garments. Jehoiachin ate bread before him continually all the days of his life.
